name: sprechstunde
description: Local state files of sprechstunde that are not in the repo.

entries.why: Holds the Mistral API key and the SIP trunk password. Neither can be read back from the provider; losing the file means issuing new keys and a new SIP password, and the agent cannot reach any model or line until then.
entries.recreate: Copy .env.example and fill in: LiveKit dev key/secret (any random pair, must match compose config), MISTRAL_API_KEY from console.mistral.ai, SIP credentials from the provider's control center.
`npm ci`, then `npm run download-files` (the turn-detector tokenizer is stored inside node_modules)
`npm run web:install` (the settings UI has its own package, web/package.json)
`npm run build` and `bash dev/i18n.sh compile` (the settings UI lands in dist/web)

Test output only: latency metrics (JSONL, numbers only; the agent container bind-mounts `var/metrics`), debug transcripts of one's own test calls in `var/transcripts` (only with SPRECHSTUNDE_TRANSCRIPT_DIR; personal data, delete once read), TTS samples in `var/samples/` (one folder per test run, e.g. `npm run tts:try` writes `<date>_tts-try`; the folder has a README), voice reference clips (`dev/record-voice.sh` re-records one, `dev/fetch-thorsten-sample.sh` re-downloads the CC0 clip). Losing it loses old measurements and one's own recording, nothing else. The exceptions are `var/settings/voice.json`, `var/profiles` and `var/db`, declared below.

entries.why: The voices and models the agent actually runs with: presets plus the active primary/fallback, written by the settings UI (`npm run admin`). Nothing else records which voice a venue was tuned to; losing it drops the line back to the SPRECHSTUNDE_TTS_* values in .env and the comparison work has to be redone by ear.
entries.recreate: Only by picking the voices again in the settings UI. Delete it and the agent runs on .env alone, so a missing file is degraded, not broken.

entries.why: The venue profiles (greeting, facts, opening hours) the settings UI picks from per call; they hold the real venue data that never goes into this repo. Losing the directory loses the only copy of those profiles and the agent falls back to the start profile.
entries.recreate: Only from the venue's own copy of each profile JSON; copy profiles/example/profile.de.json as a template.

entries.why: The knowledge database (sources, sections, revisions with their approval history and hand edits) written by the settings UI. It holds the only copy of text a venue edited by hand and of the review history; a fetched page can be fetched again, an edit cannot. `var/db/files/<tenant>/<sha256>` holds the ORIGINAL uploaded PDFs and pictures of document sources (content-addressed): an upload exists nowhere else, so losing it leaves the extracted text but not the document it came from or the means to read it again; an upload may be a venue's own document, so keep it out of the repo and out of unencrypted copies.
entries.recreate: Not reproducible: web sources can be added and fetched again, hand-written text and edits are lost. Back up var/db including its files/ directory (copy the .sqlite file while the admin is stopped, or use sqlite3 .backup); an uploaded document can only be uploaded again from the venue's own copy.

`npm run fallback` records the profile's `fallback` text with Mistral TTS (needs MISTRAL_API_KEY and, for the venue's voice, the same SPRECHSTUNDE_TTS_* as the agent). Without it Asterisk plays its English prompt.
Written only by `lk agent console --record`: audio and session reports of test conversations. Throwaway; delete after review, never back it up.
